rule.name: DRY setAttribute Calls
rule.description: When three or more consecutive setAttribute() calls target the same element, they must be refactored into a single Object.entries() loop.

rule.name: DRY Direct Property Assignment
rule.description: When three or more consecutive direct property assignments target the same element, refactor to an Object.entries() loop with bracket access.

rule.name: Cache Repeated String Literals
rule.description: String literals used more than twice in a single file must be extracted into a named constant.

rule.name: Minimal JSDoc for Functions
rule.description: Every function declaration and named function expression must have at least a one-line JSDoc summary. Do not repeat TypeScript type info. Arrow callbacks may omit JSDoc when intent is obvious.

rule.name: No Extra Blank Lines Between Related Statements
rule.description: Guard clauses, variable declarations, and closely related sequential statements must not be separated by blank lines.

rule.name: Collapse Sequential Declarations
rule.description: Two to three sequential const/let/var assignments should be merged using the comma operator. Skip if readability would suffer.

example.before: const content = targetElement.innerHTML; const m = content.match(/^[\s\n\t\r]*[0-9]+</);

rule.name: Bracketless One-Liners
rule.description: Single-statement if/else blocks must omit curly braces. Prefer short-circuit for guard+call, ternary for symmetric branches.

sub-rule.description: Guard clause + single function call → short-circuit
Symmetric if/else with single calls → ternary

rule.name: IIFE Try/Catch Wrapper
rule.description: Every IIFE that starts a TypeScript route or page file must wrap its entire body in try/catch. The catch block must log a clean diagnostic message identifying the failed module.

rule.name: Prefer Performant DOM Queries
rule.description: Use the cheapest DOM query that fulfils the need. Only replace querySelector/querySelectorAll when the replacement is measurably faster and does not change semantics.

notes.note: MutationObserver and IntersectionObserver are optional — use only when demonstrably beneficial.
Benchmark before switching query methods; pick the more performant option.

performance.rule: Always benchmark before choosing between two implementation approaches.

rule.name: Cache Hard-Coded Strings & RegExps
rule.description: String literals used 2+ times must be stored as a const at the nearest common scope. RegExp instances must always be cached at module/scope level. Cross-file shared strings go in .constants.ts inside a deep-frozen Record (Object.freeze({...} as const)).

rule.name: Convert Sequential Procedures to Iterative
rule.description: Repetitive sequential calls (appendChild chains, .style assignments, jQuery .removeClass) must be converted to loops or combined calls.

sub-rule.description: Sequential appendChild → for...of over parent-child pairs

rule.name: Guard Event Listeners with Dataset Checks
rule.description: Before addEventListener, check el.dataset.<name>Bound. Set it to "1" after binding to prevent duplicate registrations.

rule.name: Inline Single-Use Values
rule.description: Variables assigned once and used once should be inlined. Exception: when the variable name significantly clarifies complex logic.

example.before: const content = targetElement.innerHTML; const m = content.match(RE);

rule.name: Vendor File Header Marker
rule.description: All third-party / vendor / bundle files living inside ts/src/ must carry the header comment '// # ! VENDOR FILE — DO NOT EDIT' on the first non-empty line. The path must also be excluded from tsconfig.json and eslint.config.mjs.

rule.name: ESLint Migration-Phase Disabled Rules
rule.description: During the JS → TS migration the following rules are intentionally disabled to suppress thousands of false-positive warnings from idiomatic DOM null-guard patterns. Re-enable after full retyping.

disabled.reason: ~1100 false positives from defensive if(el)/if(str) null-guards
~1300 false positives from truthy checks on runtime-nullable values

rule.name: Async Function Return Types
rule.description: Async functions must use Promise<void>, never bare void (tsc error TS1064). Non-async void functions should annotate : void. Functions returning a value with a complex inferred type should use eslint-disable-next-line for explicit-function-return-type.

example.after: // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/explicit-function-return-type function getMsg(key: string) { return messages[key] ?? key; }

rule.name: eslint-disable Usage Rules
rule.description: eslint-disable-next-line must be used sparingly and correctly. Never place inside template literals. Combine multiple rules in one comment. Add a reason when non-obvious. Prefer fixing root cause.

sub-rule.description: Never place eslint-disable inside template literals — it becomes text
